topics.title: Functions of Several Variables, 3D Geometry & Surfaces
topics.explanation:
In single-variable calculus you studied \( y = f(x) \). In multivariable calculus a function \( z = f(x, y) \) takes two independent inputs and produces one output.

Visual analogy: Your position on the ground is \( (x, y) \) and the height of the terrain at that point is \( z = f(x, y) \). The graph is a 3D surface.

Domain & Range: Domain is a region in the \( xy \)-plane. Range is the set of possible \( z \)-values.

Example: \( f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 \) forms a paraboloid. At \( (0,0) \) the value is 0; at \( (1,2) \) the value is 5.

questions.question: Describe the surface represented by \( z = x^2 + y^2 \). What is the value at the point \( (1, 2) \)?
What is the domain of the function \( f(x, y) = \sqrt{1 - x^2 - y^2} \)?

topics.title: Limits & Continuity in Higher Dimensions
topics.explanation:
In 2D limits you approach a point from only left or right. In 3D you can approach \( (a,b) \) along infinitely many paths. A limit exists only if the function approaches the same value along every path.

Path test to show a limit does not exist:

  1. Substitute \( y = mx \).
  2. If the result still depends on \( m \), the limit does not exist.

Worked example: \( \lim_{(x,y)\to(0,0)} \frac{xy}{x^2 + y^2} \). Along \( y = mx \) the limit is \( \frac{m}{1+m^2} \). Different values of \( m \) give different results, so the limit does not exist.

Continuity of piecewise functions: At a boundary point, left-hand limit = right-hand limit = function value.

questions.question: Show that \( \lim_{(x,y)\to(0,0)} \frac{xy}{x^2 + y^2} \) does not exist.
questions.solution: Along y = mx the limit becomes m/(1+m²), which depends on m. Hence the limit does not exist.

questions.question: Find A so that \( f(x) = \begin{cases} A + x & x < 2 \\ 1 + x^2 & x \ge 2 \end{cases} \) is continuous at x = 2.
questions.solution: LHL = A + 2, RHL = 5. Set equal: A = 3.

topics.title: Partial Derivatives & Clairaut’s Theorem
topics.explanation:
When finding \( f_x \), treat y as constant. When finding \( f_y \), treat x as constant.

Example: For \( f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 + x^2 y^2 \)

  • \( f_x = 2x + 2x y^2 \)
  • \( f_y = 2y + 2x^2 y \)

Clairaut’s Theorem: If the second partials are continuous, then \( f_{xy} = f_{yx} \).

questions.question: If \( f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 + x^2 y^2 \), find all first-order partial derivatives.
Verify Clairaut’s theorem for \( u = \ln(x^2 + y^2) \).

topics.title: Multivariable Chain Rule & Total Differentials
topics.explanation:
Single parameter case (\( x = x(t), y = y(t) \)):

\( \frac{dz}{dt} = f_x \frac{dx}{dt} + f_y \frac{dy}{dt} \)

Two parameter case (\( x = u+v, y = u-v \)):

\( z_u = f_x + f_y \), \( z_v = f_x - f_y \)

Total differential coefficient under constraint: Use implicit differentiation to find \( \frac{dy}{dx} \), then substitute into the total derivative formula.

questions.question: Find the total differential coefficient of \( u = x^2 y \) w.r.t. x where \( x^2 + xy + y^2 = 1 \).

topics.title: Homogeneous Functions & Euler’s Theorem
topics.explanation:
A function \( f(x,y) \) is homogeneous of degree \( n \) if \( f(tx, ty) = t^n f(x,y) \).

Euler’s Theorem: If \( u \) is homogeneous of degree \( n \), then

\( x u_x + y u_y = n u \)

This is a frequently asked proof question (5 marks).

questions.question: State and prove Euler’s theorem on homogeneous functions.
questions.solution: Standard proof using u = xⁿ F(y/x) and partial differentiation.

questions.question: Verify Euler’s theorem for \( u = \frac{x^3 + y^3}{x + y} \).

topics.title: Gradient, Directional Derivatives & Extrema
topics.explanation:
The gradient of a scalar field \( \Phi(x,y,z) \) is

\( \nabla \Phi = \Phi_x \mathbf{i} + \Phi_y \mathbf{j} + \Phi_z \mathbf{k} \)

Directional derivative in the direction of unit vector \( \hat{u} \) is \( \nabla \Phi \cdot \hat{u} \).

For extrema of \( f(x,y) \), solve \( f_x = 0 \), \( f_y = 0 \) and use the second derivative test with \( \Delta = f_{xx} f_{yy} - (f_{xy})^2 \).

questions.question: Find the gradient of \( \Phi = 3x^2 y - y^3 z^2 \) at the point (1, −2, −1).
Find the directional derivative of \( f(x,y,z) = xy + yz + zx \) at (1,2,3) in the direction of the vector 2i + 3j + 6k.
